name: progressive-blur
title: Progressive Blur
description: Adds a masked blur band to the top, bottom or both edges of a scroll area. Stacked blur layers fade from sharp to heavy, so photos or rows melt away instead of being cut off.
use: Scrollable galleries or lists need a soft edge so the content seems to continue.
avoid: It blurs real content under the band, so controls or text at that edge become hard to read.
a11y: The band is decorative and pointer-transparent, but it fades real content with no contrast or reduced-motion consideration. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A rounded photo panel headed "Camera roll" over a three-column grid of square shots. Near the bottom edge the photos soften into a heavy blur that melts into the panel background, hiding the last row.
behaves: The blur band stays fixed while the photo grid scrolls beneath it, fading lower content out rather than cutting it. There is no animation of its own and it never reacts to the pointer.
customise: Position (top, bottom or both), band height, blur levels and a class name are props; the band itself holds no content.
weight: moderate: Eight stacked backdrop-blur layers over the band; static but costly to composite.
demo: Header "Camera roll", "1,284 photos, synced 2 min ago" and a grid of varied square photos.
issues: The band blurs content under it, so anything at the bottom edge becomes unreadable.
The children prop is accepted but never rendered, so it has no effect.
polishWhy: The fade is smooth and reads as a scroll cue; blurring live content hides it.
